Sometimes a Caterpillar rushes two squares on its very first move, right past an enemy Caterpillar standing beside it. That's not quite fair — so, just this once, the enemy Caterpillar may capture it anyway, as if it had only moved one square. This is called "en passant" (French for "in passing"), and it only works right away, the very next move.

Some games end in a draw — nobody wins! Stalemate is one way: no legal move, but not in check. A game is also a draw when there isn't enough material left to checkmate (like a lone king against a lone king), if the exact same position happens three times in a row, or if 50 moves pass with no capture and no pawn move.
